reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: updateEntityColumn on one of 1 roots, then channel.flush(); one effect declaring all 1 root slots sums them
reading.floor: one of 1 alien signals written with no batch; one alien effect reads and sums all of them
reading.caveat: ONE OPERATION IS ONE WRITE TO ONE OF 1 ROOTS, chosen round-robin, AND ONE SETTLE; one effect reads every root and sums them. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: declared against auto-tracked dependencies, measured as what each read inside a run costs. Ours declares the 1 root slots as the effect's sources once, at build; a run checks each source stamp before the body and the body reads each entity, and nothing is re-linked. Alien-signals has no declaration: every run re-tracks, each read of a signal inside the body checks or re-creates its dependency link, and the run is synchronous at the end of the write, so there is no settle call. EXPECTED DIRECTION [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]: the per-read cost of re-tracking grows with the number of roots on alien, so the ratio is expected to fall as the root count grows, if re-tracking costs more per read than the stamp check ours does per source. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
